resources.string: Enter the address of the MongoDB database your Nightscout uses. A read-only database user is enough. The address is stored encrypted on this phone.
No glucose entries found. Check the database name.
Synced. Asked for %4$d stretches of time and checked %1$d readings, %2$d treatments and %3$d insulin-on-board records. Only missing or recent data is requested.
Set up the Nightscout connection on the Connection tab, then sync.
Less than 70%% of readings are available for this period, so these numbers may not represent it well.
No readings in this period. Sync to load them.

Save everything this app holds (the connection and all stored readings) to one encrypted file, and restore it later, for example after reinstalling. Keep the file somewhere safe, and remember the passphrase: it cannot be recovered. Restoring adds readings and never deletes any.
At least %1$d characters. Needed to restore.
Backup saved. %1$d readings and the connection are in it.
The saved connection was restored. Check it on the Connection tab.
The backup had no connection, so the current one was kept.
No treatments in this period. Sync to load them.
%1$d meals, %2$s g carbs per day on average
Bolus insulin %1$s U in total, %2$s U per day (includes automatic micro-boluses, not basal)
How glucose behaves at different times of day. This describes what happened; it does not suggest changes to your settings.
Only %1$d days of data (at least %2$d needed), so no pattern is shown.
Meals are carb entries of 5 g or more, with entries within 30 minutes merged. Meals eaten while glucose was already low are left out.
Only %1$d meals (at least %2$d needed), so no pattern is shown.
Above range 2 hours after: %1$d of %2$d meals
Low within 4 hours after: %1$d of %2$d meals
No readings in this period. Sync to load them.
This is right now. Touch and slide a finger across the chart to see any earlier moment.

Top: glucose, with orange dots for carbs (up to 14 days). Bottom: basal in teal (lighter where it is the profile in force, with its percentage and time shift applied) and insulin boluses as blue bars (lighter for automatic micro-boluses), each with its own scale.
No glucose reading near this time
No basal information for this time
Last 3 hours: %1$s g carbs, %2$s U bolus

One chart: glucose line, basal as the teal area along the bottom (its own scale, labelled at the top of the area; lighter where it is the profile in force, with its percentage and time shift applied), carbs as orange circles and insulin boluses as blue triangles on the glucose line (smaller and lighter for automatic micro-boluses). Amounts are written next to them for periods up to 2 days.
Part of this period has not been synced yet. Press Sync now to fill it in; only the missing part is requested.
No insulin-on-board data for this time
Purple line: insulin on board as reported by the loop, on its own scale (shown on the overlaid layout; the moment card shows it for both).
Nightscout returned nothing for these days

How often the closed loop ran a higher or lower basal than your profile schedule, from the temp basals it set. Percentages are of the time a temp basal was running. The baseline is the profile that was in force at each moment, including any percentage and time shift (AAPS switch records).
Loop data covers %1$s%% of this period.
Loop data covers only %1$s%% of this period (temp basals are missing for the rest), so these numbers describe part of it.
Basal insulin per day: %1$s U vs %2$s U on profile
%1$d temp basals (%2$s a day): %3$d above, %4$d below, %5$d at profile when set
Dashed amber lines mark profile switches, with the profile name and any percentage or time shift; a lighter band shows how long a temporary switch lasted.
No profile switches in this period. The comparison uses the profile in force when the period began.
